title: Typed event rehydration runner with checkpointed TTL and deterministic dedupe
creator: Aisha Berman
description: Build a reusable, schema-aware rehydration runner to reingest historical console events into the analytics pipeline. Goals: 1) ensure idempotent processing across retries and partial runs using deterministic dedupe keys, 2) checkpoint progress with TTL-safe resume tokens so long-running backfills can pause and resume without losing in-flight visibility, 3) apply event-level typing and validation so downstream aggregations and rollups do not regress when older, schema-drifted events are reprocessed. This ticket covers design, an initial PoC runner, integration tests against the staging analytics cluster, and a production-safe migration plan with a small safety window and one-way toggles.
acceptance_criteria: Runner can process a 30-day event slice (~50M events) and produce identical derived metrics compared to a golden reingestion job
Resume tokens checkpoint every 5 minutes and allow safe restart from last checkpoint without duplication
Deterministic dedupe: events ingested twice (same source+id+schema-version fingerprint) are ignored downstream
Integration test suite exercises schema evolution scenarios (field rename, optional->required) and validates fallback mappings
Runbook documented: operator steps for pausing, resuming, forcing a slice to skip, and rollback instructions
infra_changes: Introduce resume_token table in analytics-metadata DB (sharded by date) with TTL policy
Add dedupe-fingerprint index to raw_events subject to periodic TTL cleanup
Expose runner metrics: processed_count, checkpoint_lag_seconds, dedup_rate, error_rate
migration_notes: Start with a single customer cohort (internal dev+beta orgs) for validation, run side-by-side outputs for 48 hours, then opt-in production slice. If derived metrics differ >0.5% on critical dashboards, pause and run diagnostic diff tooling. Plan includes a fallback path that switches routing to live ingest while cleanup runs finish.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Prefer deterministic fingerprint (source|id|schema_version|normalized_payload_hash) over full payload hashing to reduce storage pressure but keep collision risk low
Checkpoint frequency set to 5 minutes: balances restart cost vs. checkpoint table load. Can be tuned per-run in config

We will validate fields via a typed mapping rather than full JSON schema validation to avoid rejecting borderline historical events; missing required fields are mapped to sentinel values and surfaced in QA dashboards
Runner will perform light-weight normalization (timestamp rounding, canonicalizing user_id formats) to improve dedupe stability; heavier normalization moved to a downstream migration job
testing_plan: Unit tests for fingerprint generation and drift-tolerant typed mappings
End-to-end replay on staging with an isolated sink to compare derived metrics against a golden export
Chaos injection: random worker restarts to validate resume semantics
Smoke run on a 48-hour slice in production beta orgs with manual QA signoff
open_questions: Should dedupe fingerprints include model_version for model-scored events? (affects dedupe granularity)
Retention TTL for resume_token table: default 30 days vs. longer for very long replays
How to present partial replays in the Console dashboards UX (marking data as rehydrated vs. live)
